design.title: Exposure-and-sharpness nuisance randomisation: every training view is re-photographed at random (brightness, contrast, gamma, colour balance, saturation, blur, sensor noise) so a pixel fingerprint of one survey stops being a usable solution
design.eli5: The model had three photographs of Berlin and learned each one by its exact brightness, colour tint and fine grain, like recognising a page by the paper it is printed on rather than by the words. A test showed it: brighten its own training photo slightly and it is lost. Now every training picture is handed to it slightly re-photographed at random each time, a bit brighter or darker, warmer or cooler, softer or sharper, grainier, so the paper keeps changing and only the words, the streets and building outlines, stay the same. If it can only pass by reading the words, it should also read a fourth photograph it has never seen.
design.hypothesis: The three-survey training signal of experiment 2 did not teach exposure invariance; it taught three exposures. Design-stage probe on experiment 2's exported berlin.onnx, scored with the frozen scorer's own 400 eval crops (numbers from the design stage, not part of the record): on its OWN training photograph truedop_2023 the model reads 0.087, but the same photograph +20 on every pixel reads 1.240 (usable 94.3% -> 14.7%), -20 reads 1.550, and a 1 px Gaussian blur reads 1.100 (median 29 m -> 253 m). That is the identical brittleness the era's founding table measured on the single-photograph champion (+20 -> 1.453, blur -> 1.271): three photographs with three different colour balances (channel means 118/121/117, 99/98/99, 117/116/110) were absorbed as three pixel-exact fingerprints, not as an invariance, and nothing in the training signal asks for one. Globally matching the held-out 2024 photograph's per-channel mean/std to truedop_2023 recovers only a fifth of the gap (1.583 -> 1.365, false fix 65% -> 47%, usable 7% -> 10%), so the rest of the gap is LOCAL: the 2024 survey is softer and lower-contrast (channel std 41/39/40 vs 50/47/43) with its own shadows, resampling and 1 m texture, and the model's fix rides exactly that 1 m texture (hence the blur result). Experiment 3 tried to forbid fingerprints at the feature level and was reverted, but its mechanism never bit: the logged cross-survey cosine was already 0.966 at epoch 1 on a freshly initialised network, because post-ReLU GAP features are non-negative and share a large common component, so a cosine floor of 0.9 was satisfied for free and the term's gradient was negligible (cons 0.065 against a cross-entropy of 2.9). Its refutation is of a vacuous constraint, not of feature invariance; a fair retest needs batch-centred features. The direct remedy for what the probe measured is the library's L2 entry #2: randomise, per training view, the nuisances that differ between exposures of the same ground (global intensity, contrast, gamma, per-channel colour balance, saturation, sharpness, sensor noise). A pixel-exact fingerprint then no longer predicts the cell across the model's own training stream, so capacity has to move to what survives those transformations, which is the layout structure at 2 m scale and up that all four surveys share. The blur component is the load-bearing one for the cross-survey question: it is the 1 m texture that is survey-specific, and the exp-2 model demonstrably depends on it. This cannot synthesise leaf-off versus canopy or a different shadow direction; the three surveys supply that part, and this experiment makes them the only route left.
